data.reasoning: Both models successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD and found it to be a standard, safe binary package that downloads pinned artifacts from official GitHub releases. The disagreement was solely due to a transient API error in the Qwen model when processing non-executable metadata files (.SRCINFO and .gitignore), which does not impact the security posture of the package.
data.disagreement_analysis: The Qwen model encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing .SRCINFO and .gitignore, leading to an inconclusive overall verdict. The Deepseek model successfully audited these files. Since these files contain no executable code, the API failure did not obscure any security risks.
coverage_issues: Qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO and .gitignore due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: The audit tool should handle transient API errors for non-executable files (like .SRCINFO or .gitignore) more gracefully. If critical executable files (PKGBUILD, .install) are successfully audited and deemed safe, missing metadata files should not force an overall 'inconclusive' verdict.
